creator: NA

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Sketches and Drawings, 11
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a sketch from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

creator: Creator:Muhammad Farhan Bin Osman
description: "This year, Muslims in Singapore celebrated Eid differently. With the stay-at-home restrictions, Muslim families are using online video telecommuting apps, such as Zoom, to celebrate the occasion. The communal prayer calls(takbir) and a live sermon were also broadcasted over radio and online channels such as YouTube and the Facebook pages of Muis and local mosques."--Contributed by Muhammad Farhan Bin Osman, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Research Process : Miscellaneous Documents, Drawings, Plans and Photographs, 35
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a sketch from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

creator: NA

Opened in 1977, it closed down in 1999. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Boxes of KitKats on a flat trolley for distribution to medical frontliners during circuit breaker period
creator: Creator:Dennis Chew Yin Sang
description: "We (Zuvelab Singapore Pte Ltd) donated 10,000 pcs of Chocolate Bar to all the frontliners of KKH, NUHS, TTSH,SGH,SKH and KTPH. Special thanks to MCCY whom help us to connect to the right personnel of different hospital. As delivery is during Covid19 Phase One. We deliver personally with our car, mask-on and pre-arrange with the staff on exact location and time to receive so as to minimise contact. Our first donation was to SGH on the 21st April 2020, follow by other hospitals base on their convenient time. We know that there are many donations/sponsorship of foods and drinks etc to the frontline workers. We would like to do our part. We wish to give them extra energy and motivation. We have bought a lot of chocolate (all are Halal certified) namely KitKat, Nestles, Kinder Bueno and Konsep and wish to give to hospital as an stimulant to all the frontline staffs and workers. Bless all frontliners for their constant and selfless contribution well."--Contributed by Dennis Chew Yin Sang, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows boxes of KitKats on a flat trolley waiting to be distributed to medical frontliners during the circuit breaker period. These chocolates are donated by Zuvelab Singapore Pte Ltd to show their appreciation for the selfless contribution of medical frontliners in the fight against COVID-19. title: Birthday card for resident of Moral Welfare Home
creator: Creator:Be Kind SG
description: Birthday card made by Be Kind SG volunteers for resident of Moral Welfare Home. "I'm Sherry, founder of Be Kind SG, a groundup movement inspiring acts of kindness via micro-volunteering and raising visibility of our 'less visible' communities. Before COVID-19, we visited both Moral Welfare Home and THK Home for Disabled at least once monthly. Since February, all volunteer visits have been suspended. Hence, we had to turn to Zoom sessions with small groups of residents per session. During each session, we will have interactive elements like Pictionary game, singing performance, and upper body exercise. We have also incorporated live streaming from our local attractions, such as Bollywood Veggies, to bring the outdoors to the residents (as they are unable to go for outings). Our regular volunteers have been supportive by doing recce trips to the local attractions prior to the Zoom session. We also engage performers for a nominal fee and our volunteer have even put up a pet segment where his dog performed some tricks for the residents. It has been quite interesting as we would not have been able to perform this pet segment at the Homes. Our last segment will usually be singing a birthday song and we will send handcrafted birthday cards over for the residents. We also send some tea time refreshments to the residents once monthly for them to enjoy after our Zoom sessions. We hope to be able to resume in-person volunteering soon."--Contributed by Be Kind SG, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

creator: Creator:Elisa Liu
description: "Artist's note: 'A Moment in Time' is a visual journal project capturing a local artist's perspective on today's changing world and the challenging times we face today. Containing ephemera collected from different sources - newspaper clippings, photographs, cut-outs from brochures and magazines, this project juxtaposes newsmaking headlines with the artist's own thoughts and observations. Since January this year, Elisa has been collating and assembling pages and pages of collage and narrative, aiming to create one book of curated perspective a month. Each journal spread has been arranged aesthetically and thoughtfully - a visual treat for the viewer, and an invitation to contemplate the moments passed and the times ahead. The goal of this project is to create a documentation of life from today's perspective - in a genuine and aesthetic way. I first had to devise a systematic way of collecting and sorting the various ephemera, which was done through a series of L-shaped files. At the end of each month, I will batch the ephemera according to topic, and trim the elements that will go into the journal. During the creation of the collage, time is taken to plan and compose each spread. The collage is then assembled and embellished with details. The process is ongoing, and I hope to create 12 such journals (one for each month) by the end of the year."--Contributed by Elisa Liu, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows clippings on the state of emergency declared in Malaysia due to the increasing infection cases during the Covid-19 pandemic. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

creator: NA

abstract: சாந்தா ரதி ஒரு பன்முகத்தன்மை கொண்டவர். அவர் ஒரு நடனக் கலைஞர், ஆசிரியர், நடன இயக்குனர், கலாச்சார ஆர்வலர் மற்றும் திரைப்படத் தயாரிப்பாளர். அவர் இந்தியா மற்றும் சிங்கப்பூரின் மிகச் சிறந்த நடன குருக்களின் கீழ் பிரத்தியேக பயிற்சி பெற்றவர். Photos capture the making of documentary film And miles to flow. It highlights the kinship in spirit shared by Kathakali of India with Noh and Kabuki of Japan and Chinese Opera with Kathakali occupying the centre stage. She has scripted, directed and produced the film. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Model, 2
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the model of the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Seletar East Camp during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.SELETAR EAST CAMPAs part of the national effort to stem the spread of COVID-19 in the dormitories, healthy migrant workers were moved into unused Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) camps. Seletar East Camp was one of these camps. Working closely with the SAF, #TeamNUH quickly operationalised a medical post in this camp in May 2020 within 72 hours. The team also carried out swabbing and serology work there. The team ceased operations at the camp on 8 July 2020."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Orthogonal Model, 1
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the orthogonal model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Tuas South Community Care Facility (CCF) during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.TUAS SOUTH COMMUNITY CARE FACILITYSet-up at a repurposed factory site in Tuas South, #TeamNUH received our first COVID-19 patient at the Community Care Facility (CCF) on 16 May 2020. It was set up as part of the national effort to house migrant workers who tested positive for COVID-19, present with mild symptoms and at low risk of needing acute hospital care. #TeamNUH was stationed at the CCF 24/7 to provide medical care and support for the migrant workers. Among the initiatives and processes rolled out, the residents were taught to monitor their own vital signs, achieving 100% compliance in this version of telemedicine, enabling the team to detect early signs of worsening illness."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Former Jinricksha Station, 2007 : general view [1]
creator: Tay, Lionel
description: This is a 2007 photograph showing a general view of the former Jinrickshaw (also spelt as jinricksha) Headquarters located at the junction of Neil Road and Tanjong Pagar Road. The Ionic pilasters and curved pediment on the corner, the square tower with its octagonal dome and arches on the building’s lower level are some of the architectural features seen in the picture. Built in 1903, the Jinrickshaw Station, also known as the Jinriksha Station, served as the registration centre for rickshaws. In the late 1980s, it was included in the Tanjong Pagar Conservation Area and refurbished by the Urban Development Authority (URA) to house shops and restaurants today. Coloured shop signages are seen on the building’s façade. High-rise buildings are also seen in the background. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Various Parts of the Model, 104
creator: NA
description: This photograph taken by Albert Lim shows parts of the model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Sarimbun Scout Camp : Scouts, 9
creator: NA
description: Scouts at the Sarimbun Scout Camp located at Jalan Bahtera, off Lim Chu Kang Road. This 12-hectare campsite provides a rural enclave for local scouts. Its design is reminiscent of the ambiguous boundaries associated with vernacular kampong architecture. Completed in phases from 1986 to 1996 by Akitek Tenggara, with Tay Kheng Soon leading the design team, the campsite was initially made up of an assembly hall, a canteen, a dormitory, and 3 washrooms. In the later years, more structures were added, including a 7-storey high steel tower and A-frame timber huts.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Co-ordinating Rules, 14
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a co-ordinating rules drawing from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Virtual lessons during circuit breaker period [2]
creator: Creator:Ricky FM Law
description: "COVID's Impact on Education and Training — Survival Tips After decades of teaching, because of COVID-19, I am a student on online teaching tools. I had to learn three tools in two weeks. Without knowing them well, I started to use them to teach. Scary. An unprepared lecturer to conduct lessons online. How can I deliver a good lecture and ensure the students will learn well? My years of teaching experience in a classroom suddenly leave me blank. Since April 2020, I have been conducting lectures to students of RMIT University and University of London, working adults of Singapore Institute of Retail Studies, attendants to a Crisis Management Workshop, seniors and families to Silver Talks organised by the Singapore University of Social Sciences, People’s Association and Sport Singapore and members of Sunshine Seniors over an event “Dinner in the Air”. A total of over 50 hours online talk and chat in 6 weeks. What an experience! I have done online sharing and presentations during my corporate days. But not so frequently and varied in topics. Before I could do the online training starting in April, I need to learn 3 different online conference tools as different institutions use different softwares. It is by itself a challenge. After speaking to hundreds of people online in 6 weeks using different conference tools, I would like to share my experience and observations with people who need to be online. As the new normal will be delivering messages online. To be competent on online delivery, one needs to prepare oneself on three fronts, mentally, psychologically and technically. 1. Mentally - No Change. No Gain. Have you accepted the new normal of online delivery? Or are you still blaming the virus and complaining about the inconvenience of the switch? We can continue to accuse the world, the government and the virus while we reluctantly move online. With this mentality, the hurdle is so high that we might not be able to jump over it and take ourselves higher in the career growth. Only when we reframe ourselves to embrace the change and set our minds to learn and master this online skill would we be able to see the beauty of online and perform brilliantly on it. No change. No gain. 2. Psychologically - Losing Control to Creating Engagement Once we have mentally and cognitively adjusted, we need to manage our psyche and emotions. Conducting an online lecture conjures up different emotions different from a physical lecture. We talk alone for hours. I conducted 3-hour online lectures and I am going to deliver 7-hour full day lectures. We are talking to tens or even hundreds of people, but we are physically isolated and feel alone. Most of us are not DJ-trained. DJs talk for hours day in and day out. Before coming to Singapore, I worked for Radio Television Hong Kong. I know DJs. I know their work. In contrast, we are online immigrants. Some of us are the new kids on the block. Are our attendants listening? Are they learning? How to manage the emotions when nobody answers our questions? We are by ourselves. How to maintain a positive attitude with a high spirit to complete the lecture with flying colours? Do you know? Can you adapt? 3. Technically — Learn and Perform We can divide this discussion into hard and soft skills. For hard skills, it is straight forward. Learn the tool. I learnt 3 online conference tools in one week and used them in the following week to teach. It was tough. I reframe myself to create a narrative that these tools will help me shine and do a great job online which will be the new normal. Once I have mastered these tools, I can expand my training career in no time. Then I reinforce this perception with data which indicates that the market size of online education will reach US$315B by 2025 and for MOOC (Massive Online Open Course), over US$20.8B by 2023. A great potential. It is time to equip myself. Another set of hard skills is lighting and shooting environment. When we teach online, we are performing, not only teaching. It is essential for us to master the basics of 3-point lighting and basic camera shooting composition, design a basic set and ensure a quiet environment. This is to make us look good, sound good and perform well. We may want to purchase some lights, decorate a corner in the house and practise some sessions with friends to get feedback. The pointers are simple. Do not appear in the dark. Do not speak in the dark. Do not appear dull. For soft skills, how to engage attendants? How to incite participations? How to look after everybody on the call? In classroom management, we learn about using eye-contact and physical distance to engage students. How to replicate that online? How to use your voice? Do you know how to use your mic? When to stop for a break during the lecture? How many breaks? I normally let attendants in 5-10 minutes before the call depending on the class size. I play music while they are waiting. I put up a white board asking them to draw their emotions on how they feel today. I welcome and chat with them through the chat box. These are examples of my ice-breakers. When we start, I ask them whether they like my music. The answers are not important. This is simply a warm-up to the class. Then the lesson begins. We need to set ground rules and expectations. We need to prevent interruptions. We introduce a break in relation to the complexity of the content. If it is heavy, we allow more breaks. Otherwise we charge on. I use polls, Mentimeter and Kahoot to add fun and variety to engage the attendants. There are other education tools you can use."--Contributed by Ricky FM Law, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a screenshot of a virtual dinner held during the circuit breaker period. During circuit breaker, in-person meetings were prohibited. On the screen are still shots of members of the "Sunshine seniors" who are meeting online over dinner. Description by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Model Making Photographs, 7
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the model making process for the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Raffles College building : general view [20]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1995 photograph shows the exterior of a bungalow used by the former Raffles College at the Bukit Timah Road campus. It is one of the 5 Art Deco bungalows gazetted for conservation. Established on this site in 1929, Raffles College (with King Edward VII College of Medicine) was incorporated as the University of Malaya in 1949. In 1962, this university became known as the University of Singapore, and later renamed the National University of Singapore (N.U.S.) when it merged with Nanyang University in 1980. Today, this campus is home to the N.U.S.'s Law Faculty, the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy and five Research Institutes. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Journal entry of a six-year-old during stay-home notice (SHN) [1]
creator: Creator:Tan Kai Li
description: "This photograph shows a 6-year-old's journal entry. Having returned to Singapore from the US, our family of 4 was to fulfil our Stay Home Notice (SHN) at a designated hotel. As we have young children with us, we prepared for the SHN as though we were preparing for a ''glamping" trip. In order to minimise mess from mealtimes and to ensure we could be as comfortable "living" in the hotel room as possible, we packed extra portable furniture and a whole luggage full of activities, worksheets, craft materials to keep the kids occupied. We had some unwanted roommates (i.e. cockroaches) for the first week of our stay. However, we understood that this was probably unavoidable since hotel rooms were not designed for extended stay without regular housekeeping anyway. The hotel did their best to rectify the problem, but it still took a while before we stop seeing any more roaches. Despite that, our spirits were kept high by the ability to order in our local delights and hawker fares to satisfy our cravings -- something we had missed dearly during our time in the US. Over time, as we recovered from our jetlag, we also turned the hotel room into a classroom filled with painting, clay works, games, learning exercises etc. We are grateful for the comfortable stay, delicious meals and clean linens the hotel staff had worked diligently to provide us. And despite having to stay indoors for 2 weeks, the kids had adjusted well. We also understood from the hotel staff that they were thankful for the SHN bookings as the lack of tourists meant the hotel staff would otherwise be out of work. It takes immense vision, coordination and trust in our system for the SHN arrangements to be affected so seamlessly. Having witnessed how haphazard the Covid19 management was in the States, we are really thankful to be home."--Contributed by Tan Kai Li, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a journal entry by a six-year-old during her stay home notice (SHN) with her family at a hotel. All returning Singaporeans had to serve two weeks of SHN during the pandemic. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Lee Kip Lin's House : General View, 14
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing parts of Lee Kip Lin's House. Located in Binjai Park, the house was designed by Lee and built in 1973. It has been designated as a modernist tropical house. From the street, the 353 square metres is unassuming, with its white-painted brick and plaster walls, and sloping, red-tiled roof. But from within, the house showcases its tropical architectural elements. For instance, it boasts a high ceiling with exposed timber beams and rafters. It also has unobstructed, seamless access to the living room, dining room, veranda and garden. The open layout draws in natural light and breeze to create a spacious and airy feel, making the interior seem larger than it is and more importantly cooling.

title: Sri Krishnan Temple, 2004 : exterior [2]
creator: Tan, Bonny
description: Sri Krishnan Temple (a.k.a Sri Krishna Temple), on Waterloo Street was established in 1870 on the very same site when Hanuman Beem Singh set up an idol of Sri Krishna under a banyan tree. It is the only South Indian Hindu temple in Singapore dedicated exclusively to Sri Krishna and his consort Rukmini. As Sri Krishnan Temple is located near to the Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho Temple, it also receives many Chinese Buddhist devotees who simply walk over and light joss sticks. Other than serving the religious needs of the Hindu community, Sri Krishnan temple is also a harmonious symbol of the multi-cultural and multi-religious society in Singapore. The photograph is a front view of the entrance to the temple. Sculpture above the entrance depicts a scene from a Hindu epic. The figures in relief are brightly painted. A man stands in front of the temple. A portable iron barrier separates the temple's entrance from what looks like a metal table, on which can be seen an urn with joss sticks. An umbrella on a stand shelters the urn. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Central courtyard plaza at Duo Residences during circuit breaker period
creator: Lam, Benjamin
description: "I am Benjamin Lam, I run my own business and work from home for the last 10 yrs. I live in Lavender area and walk twice daily around the area with my wife and 2 fur kids, usually around Jalan Besar, Beach Road and City Hall area. These photos that I am submitting are taken sometime 12 to 16 April , the early days of CB in the city area after office hours. I read many CB stories on Facebook by my friend in heartlands and thought it be nice to show the deserted city area during the CB period. You can see that it is awfully quiet. It was not late at all, around 6 to 7pm when the pictures were taken and the sun has not fully set. My 2 dogs can finally explore the city! You can really appreciate the colors and architecture of Kampong Glam. On normal days, it is packed and noisy with music from the many pubs and restaurants. I also notice many residential units in the iconic Duo Residence with the lights on. On normal days, they will be dark and you would think these units are unsold or unoccupied. There is hardly any vehicle on the road, almost like a scene out of a zombie apocalypse movie..."--Contributed by Benjamin Lam, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows the empty central courtyard plaza at Duo Residences during the circuit breaker period. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Wind Tunnel Test, 12
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a wind tunnel test being conducted as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Floor Plan, 6
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the floor plan of a unit from the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Sri Mariamman Temple, before renovation : exterior
creator: Kouo, Shang-Wei, 1924-1988
description: This is a black and white photograph of the Sri Mariamman Temple located at 244 South Bridge Road, before it was renovated. First built in 1827, the Sri Mariamman Temple is the oldest Hindu temple in Singapore and was popularly known as Mariamman Kovil or Kling Street Temple. The temple is dedicated to the goddess Mariamman, known for her power in curing illness and diseases. As the present six-tiered gopurum was built in 1925 and restored with elaborate figures of sculptures in the 1960s, the photograph would probably be of the temple after the restoration as three-dimensional figurative sculptures of gods and goddesses and mythological beasts can be seen. Palm leaves are tied to both sides of door of the entrance of the temple. Two sepoy soldiers wearing khaki uniforms are on guard on the boundary walls of the temple. The top of the boundary wall that surrounds the compound is lined with sculptures of cows (considered sacred by Hindus). Two women can be seen along the road outside the front entrance of the temple. The younger woman is garbed with a top and a sarong like long skirt, while the other older woman is in a samfu. A man riding on a bicycle and a motor car can be seen on the road. Overhead, power cable criss-cross from a power cable pole. Title devised by library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Wind Tunnel Test, 14
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a wind tunnel test being conducted as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Aerial view of Fort Canning and Stamford Road, 2005
creator: NA
description: This aerial photograph shows Fort Canning and Stamford Road area. Starting from the bottom left is the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce building with its distinctive Chinese green glazed roof. Across the road which is Hill Street, is the Church of St Gregory, with its white walls and spire. Moving up Hill Street to the right, is Stamford Court, which sits at the junction of Hill Street and Stamford Road. Next to it along Stamford Road is the former Malaya Publishing House (MPH) building. Further up Stamford Road, the Fort Canning Tunnel (FCT) construction and the revamp of the National Museum can be seen. The tunnel entrance and the surrounding area was once the land that housed the old National Library building. Further up the hill next to the tunnel, Fort Canning Park is visible with its manicured lawn surrounded by greenery and the large colonial building which was once the British Far East Command Headquarters during World War II. It was converted to Hotel Fort Canning in 2010. Title devised by Library staff. Description by Library staff.

title: Lim Tze Peng : calligraphy
creator: Lim, Tze Peng, 1923-
description: Relatively large in size, this calligraphic work of Lim Tze Peng was executed with the ink brush on a large sheet of paper placed on the floor. The skilled decisiveness of the artist’s execution ensures an evenness of powerful brushstrokes. Balance and harmony is achieved between the two characters in the calligraphic inscription through careful and yet spontaneous composition, demonstrating an adroit mastery of Chinese calligraphic writing. Physical dimensions of original: 1805 x 970 mm.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Various Parts of the Model, 13
creator: NA
description: This photograph taken by Albert Lim shows the model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Traditional biscuit shop at Whampoa Hawker Centre during circuit breaker period
creator: Creator:David Lim Ming Chye
description: "This picture was taken at Whampoa Hawker Centre during the Circuit Breaker around April 2020. What captured my attention was this old school biscuit shop auntie. I'd always pass by her shop when I get my dinner at the hawker centre. She's always in the same sitting position and even during the pandemic period, she was still in the same sitting position except with her mask on. It just looked so surreal to me."--Contributed by David Lim Ming Chye, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This is a photograph of a traditional biscuit shop located at the hawker centre. The photograph was taken during the circuit breaker period. A lady manning the shop can be seen wearing a face mask while waiting for customers. Biscuits in large tins can be seen behind and by the sides of the lady. Additional description by Library staff. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Landscape and Streetscape of Singapore. Marina Square Case Study, 18
creator: NA
description: This photograph of the Marina Square area was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

description: This photograph shows the Marina Bay waterfront, set against the skyline of Singapore's central business district. Also pictured is the Fullerton Building (now Fullerton Hotel), Standard Chartered Bank building (renamed as 6 Battery Road), Singapore Land Tower (SingLand Tower), UOB Building (renamed as UOB Plaza Tower 2), OUB Centre, OCBC Centre. creator: NA
description: A photograph of Chancery Lodge showing the interior of one of the condominium's townhouses. title: Town Hall, 1890s : general view
creator: Lambert, G. R.
description: This 1890s photograph shows a view of the Town Hall. Designed by John Bennett (the municipal engineer), the Town Hall was completed in 1862. This building has a theatre on the ground floor, offices and meeting rooms on the second. This Town Hall was later renamed Victoria Theatre in 1905 when Victoria Memorial Hall was built to commemorate the passing of Queen Victoria. The Memorial Hall incorporated the Town Hall (beside it) in the design, with a clock tower (built in 1906) linking the two buildings. Today, these buildings are known as the Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall and was gazetted as a national monument in 1992. Title devised by Library staff. Date of creation estimated

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Crush Waste Machine
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing a crush waste machine in the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Various Parts of the Model, 37
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Site Photographs, 54
creator: NA
description: This site photograph was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Isolation Wards, National University Hospital, during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. In the isolation wards at the National University Hospital, multidisciplinary teams work round the clock to care for patients. For these healthcare professionals on the frontline, teamwork and communication is at the core of what they do. Across wards, teams are constantly checking in with one another, ready to offer help at any time. They put patients at the centre of care."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Pharmacy, National University Hospital, during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. During the COVID-19 outbreak, outpatient pharmacies at the National University Hospital moved part of face-to-face medicine dispensing to home deliveries. To manage home deliveries, a dedicated team of pharmacists take the process of clinical checks and counselling to the phone. Pharmacy technicians oversee payment matters, and work with delivery vendors to ensure medicine is delivered on time. All this work is on top of their interactions with existing patients who still collect their medicine personally. These heroes in white coats go the extra mile just to make sure patients get the right medicine at the right time, thereby ensuring medication and patient safety."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Cheras Housing : General View, 5
creator: NA
description: A general view of the Cheras housing project in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. This development is a low-rise, low-cost housing project that Tay Kheng Soon undertook in mid-1970s. Comprising 676 two-storey houses built for the lower income groups, it is located on a 4.79 hectares site. The original sale price of each unit was M$5000 and each of them has a 13 square metres garden. The houses are arranged in straight lines to catch the prevailing wind, and are arranged in back-to-back clusters of four units around a 2.5 metre wide 'breezeway'. The project was suggested by then Prime Minister of Malaysia Tun Abdul Razak in 1975 who wanted to build low cost houses for the low income group in urban areas.

creator: Tan, Bonny
description: This is a close-up of the single-storeyed St. George's Church, showing its unplastered, orange-red brick walls. There are white louvred windows, which are semi-circular at the top, a large central one flanked by two narrow ones and two smaller windows at the sides, above each of which there is a pair of even smaller windows. Below a central white cross there are four small round windows. A small hexagonal white plaque with the words "ANNO DOMINI 1911" is mounted under the main window. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Site Photographs, 42
creator: NA
description: This photograph of Kallang Airport was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

description: This photograph shows devotees placing their offerings on a table together with a big urn with joss sticks in it at Hougang Tou Mu Kung, also known as Hougang Dou Mu temple (后港斗母宫), during the Nine Emperor Gods festival. title: Lavender Street, towards Jalan Besar, 1972 : general view
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1972 photograph shows Lavender Street, towards Jalan Besar. Lavender Street was named in 1858. At that time, the smell of the area was unbearable due to the urine and nightsoil used to fertilise the Chinese vegetable gardens. Hence, residents referred to the area as Lavender Street out of sarcasm. The name was then formalised by the Municipality. Date of creation estimated. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Conceptual still life photography (Covid-19) series: G-love our healthcare workers
creator: Creator:Priscilla Ong
description: "Hi! I'm Priscilla, a visual artist in Singapore whose photography has generally focused on travel, adventure, and architecture over the last decade or so. When leisure travel came to a complete standstill, I was creatively stifled and it took a toll on my mental health. I began to explore a different genre altogether, initiating a new outlet to channel my obsessive need to create images, starting with objects I found at home. That’s when I realised that the possibilities are endless. The lockdown also helped shape my mind about the whole idea of minimalism and what it means to be ‘more with less’; to manage with what’s available, and to find enjoyment in the little things. It was during the process of decluttering, when I came across everyday items that I could manipulate and conceptualise to give a new meaning, with the aim of provoking a reflective thought or injecting a smile. I started developing a sense of giving my attention to ordinary things and finding beauty in them. Through my art work, I’m hoping to inject a little bit of humour and colours in this otherwise challenging era of our lifetime. I’ve always been drawn to photographs that convey a simple yet powerful message in a creative manner. In this Conceptual Still Life Photography (Covid-19) Series, I hope to capture images that reflect our memories during this time."--Contributed by Priscilla Ong, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a pair of inflated white gloves. The thumbs and index fingers of the gloves have been arranged to form the shape of a heart. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Floor Plan, 9
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the floor plan of a unit from the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

creator: NA

title: Diagnostic Imaging team, National University Hospital, during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. In the current COVID-19 pandemic, the focus of the Diagnostic Imaging team at the National University Hospital (NUH) is to provide timely chest X-rays for patients. A swab test is the gold standard in diagnosing COVID-19 infection. The results are ready after 4–6 hours, while an X-ray result takes 1–2 hours in comparison. Clinical teams in the NUH Emergency Medicine Department (EMD) depend on these X-rays to decide how to manage suspect cases while waiting for swab test results. In the wards, radiographers perform chest X-rays for patients with COVID-19 infection to monitor their lung condition. These X-rays are done in the extended screening facility at EMD or by the patient’s bed in the wards using portable machines, to minimise the movement of patients. Despite the surge in the number of cases and short turnaround time, the team pressed on with fortitude and tenacity."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Dunearn Road Hostels : side view [3]
creator: NA
description: This 1992 photograph shows the side view of a two-storey Dunearn Road Hostels (DRH), at College Green along Dunearn Road. Covered walkways between buildings can be seen in the photograph. Opened in 1952 to accommodate overseas undergraduates of the then University of Malaya, the oldest hostel ceased operating in 1981. It was renamed as Sheares Hall when it relocated to the National University of Singapore campus at Kent Ridge in 1982. Title devised by Library staff.

description: This photograph shows an external front view of the Ocean Building which is under construction along Collyer Quay. Seven of the storeys that have been built are labelled. The last two storeys of the building are still covered with scaffolding, and steel piles and a large crane are seen on the topmost level. At ground level, a facade bearing the words "Ocean Building" spreads across the entrance. A long row of cars are parked outside the building's gate. The construction of this new Ocean Building involved pulling down the old Ocean Building that had stood at the site since 1923 as well as the Prince Building adjacent to it. The new building is designed to have a double convex shape with one its curved walls facing Collyer Quay and the other overlooking Raffles Place. The foundation stone of this new Ocean Building was laid on 26 March 1972 and it was completed in 1974. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Empire Colne re-named the Katong  : general view
creator: Tyers, R. K. (Ray K.), 1919-
description: This 1950s photograph shows the ship, Empire Colne sailing across the sea in Singapore. Empire Colne was a cargo ship that was built in 1944 which was later renamed Katong after being sold to Singapore. She was then sold in 1971 and renamed Greengate and then renamed Ever Glory in 1972. She was eventually scrapped in 1974. Digitized from an album page containing 7 photographs described collectively as "A life on the ocean wave". title: Award-winning photograph "Pigeons by the Singapore River"
creator: Kouo, Shang-Wei, 1924-1988
description: This photograph shows pigeons in flight, against a backdrop of financial buildings in Singapore's Central Business District (CBD). Some of the prominent buildings seen here are Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) Centre (tallest building) and United Overseas Bank (UOB) Building (octagonal building). In the foreground are bumboats on Singapore River. title: SCM Tuas Lodge during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.DORMITORY OPERATIONSNUH was tasked by the Ministry of Health to provide medical care and support at four key dormitories – Sungei Tengah Lodge, Acacia Lodge, SCM Tuas Lodge and Tuas South Dormitory. NUH teams worked closely with the nation’s FAST (Forward Assurance and Support Team) members, locum doctors and nurses, managing agents and dormitory operators round the clock to ensure the  well-being of the migrant workers. Beyond clinical care, many of NUH’s staff volunteers also donated food and fundraised to provide supplies for the migrant workers under their care. In addition, the  teams held sessions to educate our migrant worker friends on the virus and hand hygiene."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

creator: NA
description: This 1968 photograph shows the swinging doors (pintu pagar) of a house on Emerald Hill Road. These doors are a typical feature of Peranakan houses, allowing in breezes while maintaining privacy. title: Corona Ville : General View, 4
creator: NA
description: A general view of Corona Ville. Located along Jalan Lim Tai See, it is a condominium project for the middle-income housing market. The development consists of 41 houses designed in a back-to-back layout, enabling a significantly higher density than typical three-storey housing. Each house has a unique main entrance, and the arcaded facade exudes the elegance reminiscent of early modernist houses found in Singapore./ensure privacy and optimal lighting, the plan form was cleverly arranged so that the bedrooms in each house overlook the light well between the back-to-back houses rather than directly facing each other. Additionally, a 2.5-meter corridor is provided for rear access and servicing of the dwellings, while underground parking lots are available for each house.

title: Lavender Street no. 267, 1985 : exterior [1]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1985 photograph depicts a barber shop, located at no. 267 Lavender Street. Lavender Street was named in 1858. At that time, the smell of the area was unbearable due to the urine and nightsoil used to fertilise the Chinese vegetable gardens. Hence, residents referred to the area as Lavender Street out of sarcasm. The name was then formalised by the Municipality. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Sussex Estate no. 38 : general view [2]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1992 photograph shows the double-storey terrace houses at no. 38 Sussex Estate at Horsham Road. The photograph depicts three of the units. The two-storey building sits amidst green open spaces and a well laid out stone footpath serves the houses. Sussex Estate is named after the historic county of Sussex in England. The estate was developed in the mid-1950s to house the families of British senior non-commissioned officers. In 1975 when Clementi was being developed, Sussex Estate was the only pre-development feature that was retained, but was demolished later in 1997. The area where Clementi Avenue 1 is, used to be Sussex Estate. Title devised by Library staff.

creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a general view of the Institute of Technical Education in Bishan. Completed in 1993, it is made up of two parellel 250-metre-long four-storey buildings. title: Interior view of Jewel at Changi Airport during circuit breaker period [2]
creator: Creator:Regina Chan
description: "These photos were taken during circuit breaker period in May and June 2020. It shows an empty Changi Airport terminal 3, empty Jewel (in the night and day). Description/Story: From April to June 2020, the Singapore government imposed the circuit breaker in order to stop the covid 19 virus from spreading. As a result, residents were only allowed to go out for essential services such as food. On 16 May, I went to Jewel to buy back dinner. I walked through Terminal 3 in order to get to Jewel and was able to capture the empty airport. Inside T3, the normal busy check in counters were deserted and there wasn't a single soul in sight. All flights to and from Singapore were grounded. The sight broke my heart; seeing our world class airport deserted. At Jewel, the mall was empty. Restaurants were still open for business but with very few customers. I was able to grab dinner at A&W without having to queue. The famous indoor waterfall - the HSBC Rain Vortex was switched off. It made sense, as there were barely any visitors to the airport. After collecting my takeaway dinner, I headed home, while feeling a sense of sadness. As a kid, I used to enjoy watching planes take off from the viewing gallery. Covid 19 taught us not to take for granted simple moments like this. As I write this, I don't know when we will be able to see planes taking off again, but I am confident that whatever comes our way, Singapore is well able to overcome it. :) "--Contributed by Regina Chan, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows an interior view of the roof at Jewel during the circuit breaker period. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Various Parts of the Model, 68
creator: NA
description: This photograph taken by Albert Lim shows the model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Nanyang Technological University, Hall of Residence No. V : Plans and Drawings, 2
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the site location and sketches of Nanyang Technological University's Hall of Residence No. VI which is located beside Hall of Residence No. V. The latter is designed for tropical living. It is made up of four rectangular residential blocks, a foyer and a dinnig hall. Each residential block can house up to 125 students and has a central courtyard. These buildings are built with a robust concrete frame that is clearly defined. The spaces between the concrete frames are filled with glazed metal windows, which are positioned behind the frame to create partial shade. Moreover, a significant recess is incorporated beneath the windows to enable proper air circulation within the rooms. This architectural approach can be likened to the modern version of the traditional 'monsoon window' concept. While all four residential blocks share a similar basic layout, they are distinguished by the varying colors of the panels located behind the windows.

title: I Light Marina Bay, Jellight : general view
creator: NA
description: This 2010 photograph shows a lighting installation titled "Jellight" at the "I Light Marina Bay" event. Jellight is a lighting installation by Pascal Petitjean and Aamer Taher. Imagine the jellyfish deciding to leave our polluted oceans and having a refreshing dip in the clean waters of Marina Bay before escaping into the universe as 'reverse UFOs'. Hence, the installation tries to entertain and challenge all of us to be more aware of the consequences of our extravagance. The artists created these interactive and imaginative light objects, to provide an opportunity for visitors to 'grab' the jellyfish's tentacles and keep it on Earth. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Acacia Lodge during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.DORMITORY OPERATIONSNUH was tasked by the Ministry of Health to provide medical care and support at four key dormitories – Sungei Tengah Lodge, Acacia Lodge, SCM Tuas Lodge and Tuas South Dormitory. NUH teams worked closely with the nation’s FAST (Forward Assurance and Support Team) members, locum doctors and nurses, managing agents and dormitory operators round the clock to ensure the  well-being of the migrant workers. Beyond clinical care, many of NUH’s staff volunteers also donated food and fundraised to provide supplies for the migrant workers under their care. In addition, the  teams held sessions to educate our migrant worker friends on the virus and hand hygiene."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Nagore Dargah at 140 Telok Ayer Street, 1990s
creator: Liesel Strauss
description: This photograph shows the Nagore Dargah or Nagore Durgha shrine at the corner of Telok Ayer Street and Boon Tat Street. It has an Indian Muslim and classical architecture on its facade with two square pillars at each corner and a roof with repeating geometrical motifs such as small arches, circles and squares. Green pennant banners with crescent and stars motifs hang from a flag pole on the roof. "Boon Tat St" road sign can be seen on the right pillar, while "Durgha Shrine" signboard can be seen near the left pillar. Title devised by Library staff. Description by Library staff.

title: First Covid-19 swab in swabbing booth outside clinic during circuit breaker period
creator: Creator:Swabbing booth team
description: "First actual COVID-19 swab done with the booth on 26 May 2020. Frosted panels were added for patient privacy. During the COVID-19 pandemic, GPs from Public Health Preparedness Clinics (PHPCs) were asked by the Ministry of Health to do COVID-19 swabbing in their clinic premises. In mid-May 2020, our team, consisting of volunteers from Temasek International (TI) and Camry Medical Centre (CMC), a GP clinic, collaborated to design and build a swabbing booth to protect the GPs and facilitate swabbing in their clinics. The booth was manufactured by Applied Total Control Treatment Pte Ltd (ATC), a Singaporean precision engineering company, and the project was supported by Temasek Foundation. Out of this close collaboration, in less than 2 months, the booth was designed, built, tested, refined and distributed to 170 PHPCs who requested it. It has been named the COSMO SafeSwab Slim booth. It is currently being used for swabbing in clinics around the island."--Contributed by Swabbing booth team (Dr Teo Boon See, Esther Li, Michelle Evaristo, Khoo Yi-Lin, Teo Hui Keng), as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a swabbing being carried out in the swabbing booth during the circuit breaker period. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: East Coast Road no. 321, opposite Karikal Lane : general view [3]
creator: NA
description: A general view of the exterior of a single-storey house no. 321 East Coast Road (opposite Karikal Lane) is shown in this 1982 photograph. Built in Malay architectural style, the ground floor of the house is raised, and it has well-ventilated open verandah and crawl space underneath the house. It has casement windows and timber doors and a central feature is a stone staircase which leads from the ground to the raised floor of the house. The photographer's notes indicate that the owners are Chee Soon Keng and Lim Teck Lee, and the tenant has been L.M. Handy since 1927. Title devised by library staff.

title: Tuas South Community Care Facility (CCF) during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.TUAS SOUTH COMMUNITY CARE FACILITYSet-up at a repurposed factory site in Tuas South, #TeamNUH received our first COVID-19 patient at the Community Care Facility (CCF) on 16 May 2020. It was set up as part of the national effort to house migrant workers who tested positive for COVID-19, present with mild symptoms and at low risk of needing acute hospital care. #TeamNUH was stationed at the CCF 24/7 to provide medical care and support for the migrant workers. Among the initiatives and processes rolled out, the residents were taught to monitor their own vital signs, achieving 100% compliance in this version of telemedicine, enabling the team to detect early signs of worsening illness."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Birthday video call during circuit breaker period
creator: Creator:Nurann Nazurah Binte Sazali
description: "During the Circuit Breaker (CB), meeting friends physically was definitely something I missed. Much more when their birthday falls during CB. On 14 April 2020, another friend and I surprised a video call to our friend who was celebrating her birthday the moment midnight came and it was a success! We sang her "Happy Birthday" and chatted for awhile. This was our new norm. The birthday girl is the one in the blue hat."--Contributed by Nurann Nazurah Binte Sazali, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Sketches and Drawings, 37
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a sketch from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Floor Plan, 5
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the floor plan of a unit from the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Ocean Building at Collyer Quay in Singapore, 1970s [8]
creator: NA
description: This photographs shows a street and side view of the Ocean Building which is under construction along Collyer Quay, taken from an elevated angle. The view shows the convex shape of the building's facade. Steel piles and scaffoldings as well as a crane can be seen on the topmost level of the building. At street level, the construction site is cordoned off from the traffic, with signboards pasted on one section of the barrier. The rear of the site which is facing Raffles Place is heaped with construction materials, and it is also shielded by high barriers that separate it from the Mercantile Bank Chambers building opposite. The foundation stone of this new Ocean Building was laid on 26 March 1972 and it was completed in 1974. When completed, the building can be accessed either from Raffles Place or Collyer Quay. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Various Parts of the Model, 110
creator: NA
description: This photograph taken by Albert Lim shows the model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Sarimbun Scout Camp : Scouts, 5
creator: NA
description: Scouts at the Sarimbun Scout Camp located at Jalan Bahtera, off Lim Chu Kang Road. This 12-hectare campsite provides a rural enclave for local scouts. Its design is reminiscent of the ambiguous boundaries associated with vernacular kampong architecture. Completed in phases from 1986 to 1996 by Akitek Tenggara, with Tay Kheng Soon leading the design team, the campsite was initially made up of an assembly hall, a canteen, a dormitory, and 3 washrooms. In the later years, more structures were added, including a 7-storey high steel tower and A-frame timber huts.

title: SCM Tuas Lodge during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.DORMITORY OPERATIONSNUH was tasked by the Ministry of Health to provide medical care and support at four key dormitories – Sungei Tengah Lodge, Acacia Lodge, SCM Tuas Lodge and Tuas South Dormitory. NUH teams worked closely with the nation’s FAST (Forward Assurance and Support Team) members, locum doctors and nurses, managing agents and dormitory operators round the clock to ensure the  well-being of the migrant workers. Beyond clinical care, many of NUH’s staff volunteers also donated food and fundraised to provide supplies for the migrant workers under their care. In addition, the  teams held sessions to educate our migrant worker friends on the virus and hand hygiene."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: The Modern Tropical House : General View, 15
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the Modern Tropical House. Also known as King Albert Park House or the Kwan House, it has all the attributes of a well-designed house in the tropics including major living spaces which are 'open to sky', optimal orientation to catch the prevailing breezes, openess to encourage cross-ventilation, extensive use of water and planting, wide overhanging eaves, secondary shading devices and the restriction of air-conditioning only to those rooms where it is strictly necessary. This house was built for Mr Robert Kwan, the person who brought McDonalds into Singapore.

title: Grand Hotel columns : close-up
creator: NA
description: This 1986 photograph shows a close-up on the Corinthian columns of one of the buildings of Grand Hotel, located at Still Road South. The Victorian-style building has architectural features like decorative arches and plaster facade decorations. Grand Hotel, a Victorian-style complex was built in 1917 and used as a private residence by Moona Kadir Sultan, a wealthy Indian merchant. The complex was then-named Karikal Mahal, after the merchant’s hometown of Karikal in Tamil Nadu (India). Grand Hotel itself was established in 1947 and closed in 2000. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Chee Tong Temple : General View, 1
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a general view of Chee Tong Temple. Located along Hougang Avenue 3, the temple covers an area of 700 square metres and has two storeys. The first consists of a multipurpose hall and offices, while the second is for prayers. Rather than using the traditional Chinese roof form, this temple features a pyramidal roof clad in copper and topped by a glass skylight system. As the column supporting the roof are deeply recessed from the roof perimeter, it gives the impression that the roof is floating over the podium.

title: Tuas South Community Care Facility (CCF) during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.TUAS SOUTH COMMUNITY CARE FACILITYSet-up at a repurposed factory site in Tuas South, #TeamNUH received our first COVID-19 patient at the Community Care Facility (CCF) on 16 May 2020. It was set up as part of the national effort to house migrant workers who tested positive for COVID-19, present with mild symptoms and at low risk of needing acute hospital care. #TeamNUH was stationed at the CCF 24/7 to provide medical care and support for the migrant workers. Among the initiatives and processes rolled out, the residents were taught to monitor their own vital signs, achieving 100% compliance in this version of telemedicine, enabling the team to detect early signs of worsening illness."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Model, 3
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the model of the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Cheras Housing : General View, 6
creator: NA
description: A general view of the Cheras housing project in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. This development is a low-rise, low-cost housing project that Tay Kheng Soon undertook in mid-1970s. Comprising 676 two-storey houses built for the lower income groups, it is located on a 4.79 hectares site. The original sale price of each unit was M$5000 and each of them has a 13 square metres garden. The houses are arranged in straight lines to catch the prevailing wind, and are arranged in back-to-back clusters of four units around a 2.5 metre wide 'breezeway'. The project was suggested by then Prime Minister of Malaysia Tun Abdul Razak in 1975 who wanted to build low cost houses for the low income group in urban areas.

title: Takeaway drinks and desert during stay-home notice (SHN) [1]
creator: Creator:Tan Kai Li
description: "Takeaway meals delivered to hotel room. Having returned to Singapore from the US, our family of 4 was to fulfil our Stay Home Notice (SHN) at a designated hotel. As we have young children with us, we prepared for the SHN as though we were preparing for a ''glamping trip. In order to minimise mess from mealtimes and to ensure we could be as comfortable "living" in the hotel room as possible, we packed extra portable furniture and a whole luggage full of activities, worksheets, craft materials to keep the kids occupied. We had some unwanted roommates (i.e. cockroaches) for the first week of our stay. However, we understood that this was probably unavoidable since hotel rooms were not designed for extended stay without regular housekeeping anyway. The hotel did their best to rectify the problem, but it still took a while before we stop seeing any more roaches. Despite that, our spirits were kept high by the ability to order in our local delights and hawker fares to satisfy our cravings -- something we had missed dearly during our time in the US. Over time, as we recovered from our jetlag, we also turned the hotel room into a classroom filled with painting, clay works, games, learning exercises etc. We are grateful for the comfortable stay, delicious meals and clean linens the hotel staff had worked diligently to provide us. And despite having to stay indoors for 2 weeks, the kids had adjusted well. We also understood from the hotel staff that they were thankful for the SHN bookings as the lack of tourists meant the hotel staff would otherwise be out of work. It takes immense vision, coordination and trust in our system for the SHN arrangements to be affected so seamlessly. Having witnessed how haphazard the Covid19 management was in the States, we are really thankful to be home."--Contributed by Tan Kai Li, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows takeaway food for the family confined to a hotel room while serving out their stay-home notice (SHN). All returning Singaporeans had to serve two weeks of SHN during the pandemic. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Moral Welfare Home Zoom session
creator: Creator:Be Kind SG
description: Screenshot of Be Kind SG Zoom volunteering session with Moral Welfare Home. "I'm Sherry, founder of Be Kind SG, a groundup movement inspiring acts of kindness via micro-volunteering and raising visibility of our 'less visible' communities. Before COVID-19, we visited both Moral Welfare Home and THK Home for Disabled at least once monthly. Since February, all volunteer visits have been suspended. Hence, we had to turn to Zoom sessions with small groups of residents per session. During each session, we will have interactive elements like Pictionary game, singing performance, and upper body exercise. We have also incorporated live streaming from our local attractions, such as Bollywood Veggies, to bring the outdoors to the residents (as they are unable to go for outings). Our regular volunteers have been supportive by doing recce trips to the local attractions prior to the Zoom session. We also engage performers for a nominal fee and our volunteer have even put up a pet segment where his dog performed some tricks for the residents. It has been quite interesting as we would not have been able to perform this pet segment at the Homes. Our last segment will usually be singing a birthday song and we will send handcrafted birthday cards over for the residents. We also send some tea time refreshments to the residents once monthly for them to enjoy after our Zoom sessions. We hope to be able to resume in-person volunteering soon."--Contributed by Be Kind SG, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.
