title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Site Photographs, 63
creator: NA
description: This site photograph was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Handmade wooden figurines of front-line workers during the pandemic [9]
creator: Creator:Anonymous
description: "I have started to pursue a new interest in wood-craft in December 2019, in specific up cycling off-cuts or waste wood previous used for other purpose. When the circuit breaker was implemented, I wanted to do something as a tribute to front-line workers and at the same time to continue to practice my rudimentary skills in wood-craft. These endeavors turn out to be a blessing in disguise for me, keep me mentally sane and active even while staying at home and improved my skills. I also found a craft-buddy, my friend who lives in Clementi and we exchanged tips, shared pictures and keep in contact through Whatsapp. We ended up making around one hundred of such toys and gifted them to front-line workers at Tan Tock Seng hospital as our token of appreciation and in conjunction with Singapore Nurses' Day."--Contributed by Anonymous, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows four hand-made wooden figurines wearing blue uniforms and face masks. These figurines represent medical workers. Two of them are wearing lanyards while the other two look to be holding steering wheels. These figurines were given to medical workers as a token of appreciation for the work they put in during the pandemic. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Setting up of Expo Community Care Facility for COVID-19 patients before start of circuit breaker period [5]
creator: Creator:Dennis Chew Yin Sang
description: "A very tiring and emergency express work to build tentages for Singapore EXPO hall 1 to hall 10 in 3 days. Our workers have to get special clearance from MTI & MOM before we can start work during the peak of Covid19 pandemic. We had on-site recce of Singapore EXPO Hall 1 to Hall 6 on the 9th April 2020. We completed the tentage setup by 12nd April 2020. Then there is another calling to build tentage for EXPO Hall 7 to Hall 10 on the 22nd April 2020. We required urgent approval from MTI and MOM for our workers to be able to work onsite. It was a challenging time and we have to thanks Surbana Jurong Consultants Pte Ltd to expedite getting approval for us to commence work."--Contributed by Dennis Chew Yin Sang, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a close-up view of workers from Event Business Management Pte Ltd setting up a tent outside Singapore EXPO before the start of circuit breaker. The tent will serve as Expo Community Care Facility for COVID-19 patients. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Sketches and Drawings, 34
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a drawing of an overhead bridge from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

abstract: சாந்தா ரதி ஒரு பன்முகத்தன்மை கொண்டவர். அவர் ஒரு நடனக் கலைஞர், ஆசிரியர், நடன இயக்குனர், கலாச்சார ஆர்வலர் மற்றும் திரைப்படத் தயாரிப்பாளர். அவர் இந்தியா மற்றும் சிங்கப்பூரின் மிகச் சிறந்த நடன குருக்களின் கீழ் பிரத்தியேக பயிற்சி பெற்றவர். title: Former Lai Chun Yuen opera house : exterior [1]
creator: NA
description: This 1985 photograph shows a view of the façade of the former Lai Chun Yuen opera house, at the junction of Smith Street and Trengganu Street. Built in 1887, the three-storey building was originally designed in the style of a Chinese teahouse. Lattice patterned panels on some parts of the walls and shuttered windows (typical of Singapore shophouses) can be seen on the 2nd and 3rd storeys. The building shows signs of wear and tear with a patched roof and discoloured walls, and is now occupied by residents and shops. A fruit stall selling durians, with a tarpaulin canopy, foldable tables on the ground level is one such shop. High-rise commercial buildings like OCBC Centre are also seen in the background. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Tuas South Community Care Facility (CCF) during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.TUAS SOUTH COMMUNITY CARE FACILITYSet-up at a repurposed factory site in Tuas South, #TeamNUH received our first COVID-19 patient at the Community Care Facility (CCF) on 16 May 2020. It was set up as part of the national effort to house migrant workers who tested positive for COVID-19, present with mild symptoms and at low risk of needing acute hospital care. #TeamNUH was stationed at the CCF 24/7 to provide medical care and support for the migrant workers. Among the initiatives and processes rolled out, the residents were taught to monitor their own vital signs, achieving 100% compliance in this version of telemedicine, enabling the team to detect early signs of worsening illness."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Various Parts of the Model, 62
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Marina Bay Sands lit up for National Day 2020 during the pandemic
creator: Creator:Wong Ling Siew
description: "I am an avid fan of running and would go running to Marina Bay Sands Complex - a destination regarded as a key landmark that puts Singapore on the world map. I mean this spot was featured in the movie “Crazy Rich Asians”. It is to Singapore what Big Ben and Houses of Parliament is to Londoners. But when I ran past it (alone) during the depths of CB, the entire place was void of any being. It was eerily quiet. And Marina Bay Sands, stood stoically in the middle, cloaked in lights showing “SG ❤️“ in Singaporean Red. Similarly, the Singapore Art Science museum was decked with the text “SG United”, providing some company to the Marina Bay Sands complex in that eerie quietness. Seeing Marina Bay in this state brought some sadness in me. Looking at my workplace in MBFC and the sheer silence in MBS, I couldn’t help but wonder if the CBD of Singapore, as I once knew it, would ever come back. Is everything before February this year, deeply buried in the past? Do we have to brave up to this strange new world and change our way of life for good? Or is this a deep, long period of wait before normalcy returns. It reminded me of this scene in the fairytale Sleeping Beauty, when the entire Kingdom was put into a deep sleep, until a saviour shows up and wakes the Princess (and the rest of the kingdom) from their sleep. While most public areas have become noticeably quiet, the park connector outside my home became twice as busy since lockdown begun as gyms and sports facilities were closed. It had become an outdoor gym for the masses and was congested in mornings and evenings."--Contributed by Wong Ling Siew, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a night view of Marina Bay Sands, all lit up for National Day 2020 in the Singapore colours. Despite the pandemic, National Day celebrations are just as festive, albeit different, as those celebrated in non-pandemic years. Additional description by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Venice : Aerial Photographs, 27
creator: NA
description: This aerial photograph of Venice is taken for the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Raffles Square in Singapore, 1880
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a street view of two-storey commercial buildings in Raffles Square taken in 1880. It is also known as Commercial Square in the 19th century and Raffles Place, as it is known now. Merchants with offices in the area include Singapore Dispensary and John Little, a retail store that was founded by John M. Little in 1845. Several jinrikishas are parked at the edge of the street. Several Asian men and a boy can be seen standing along the road looking at the greenery on the left. Description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Joo Chiat Place, five-foot way : general view
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This is a 1982 photograph depicting the pillared five-foot way of a building at Joo Chiat Place, opposite Rambutan Road. The floor of the corridor is decorated with designs. Five foot ways date back to the time of the Colonial Government, when Stamford Raffles included this and other details in his Town Plan of 1822; the feature was eventually integral in many settlements in neighbouring British colonies, and remains a prominent element in modern architecture in Singapore. Title devised by library staff. Title devised by library staff.

title: Participants wearing Peranakan Nyonya costumes during the Living Traditions seminar [3]
creator: Liesel Strauss
description: This photograph shows three lady participants modelling the Peranakan Nyonya costumes during the seminar, "Living Traditions - Celebrating the Peranakan Lifestyle" held at the RELC auditorium on 20 November 1999. The ladies on the right and left wear kebaya and batik sarong while the lady in the middle wears a baju panjang (or long tunic) and batik sarong. She also has a ceremonial shoulder piece (or sangkut bahu) over her left shoulder. All three are wearing the traditional Peranakan beaded shoes. The seminar was held in conjunction with the 12th Baba Convention that took place in Singapore between 19 and 21 November 1999. Title devised by Library staff. Description by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Kampong Bugis DGP/SIA Presentation, 3
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the plans and documents of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) used in a presentation. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Sarimbun Scout Camp : Scouts, 6
creator: NA
description: Scouts at the Sarimbun Scout Camp located at Jalan Bahtera, off Lim Chu Kang Road. This 12-hectare campsite provides a rural enclave for local scouts. Its design is reminiscent of the ambiguous boundaries associated with vernacular kampong architecture. Completed in phases from 1986 to 1996 by Akitek Tenggara, with Tay Kheng Soon leading the design team, the campsite was initially made up of an assembly hall, a canteen, a dormitory, and 3 washrooms. In the later years, more structures were added, including a 7-storey high steel tower and A-frame timber huts.

description: This photograph shows the grave of Bridget Catherine Beatrice Handy Chelvanathan at the Bidadari Christian Cemetery. The headstone is a big black rectangular marble slab that has the portrait of the interred at the top and some inscription underneath from her son. A stone cross is at the foot of the headstone. title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : Floor Plan, 1
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the floor plan of a unit from the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Diner posing for photograph in front of food stall at Newton Food Centre during circuit breaker period
creator: Kurniawan, Lisa
description: "Meet my food heroes!! These are just a few of the ‘uncles’ and ‘aunties’ who work day in and day out at Newton Food Centre. I moved to Singapore 12 years ago and I quickly learnt that part of the ‘requirement’ to be a true Singaporean (resident) is to be utterly crazy about FOOD!! Happy to say that I fit in quite well ? As you know this city’s landscape has evolved tremendously over the years, but some do stay the same and have become the constant in making this place feels like home, especially to me. Food centers typically are located the heart of local communities and they often take center stage in our daily lives with our families and friends. You can usually get some local grub at pretty much any time of the day (and night). But unfortunately all has suddenly changed since the start of Singapore’s Circuit Breaker period 6 weeks ago. During this trying time, most of these humble heroes are struggling and they need our help. Mask-up and head over to your nearest Hawker Centre and bring home your favorite dishes to be enjoyed with your family. Any little effort will help tremendously to ensure their survival. Let’s do what we can to support each other through this difficult time and most importantly let’s stay #sgunited"--Contributed by Lisa Kurniawan, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a diner in face mask posing for a photograph in front of a food stall at Newton Food Centre during the circuit breaker period. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Orthogonal Model, 20
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the orthogonal model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Seletar East Camp during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.SELETAR EAST CAMPAs part of the national effort to stem the spread of COVID-19 in the dormitories, healthy migrant workers were moved into unused Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) camps. Seletar East Camp was one of these camps. Working closely with the SAF, #TeamNUH quickly operationalised a medical post in this camp in May 2020 within 72 hours. The team also carried out swabbing and serology work there. The team ceased operations at the camp on 8 July 2020."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

creator: NA
description: This 1985 photograph shows the former Lai Chun Yuen opera house, at the junction of Smith Street and Trengganu Street. Built in 1887, the three-storey building was originally designed in the style of a Chinese teahouse. The building shows signs of wear and tear with a patched roof and discoloured walls, and is now occupied by residents and shops. Pedestrians, a cyclist and vehicles form part of the street scene near the former opera house. High-rise commercial buildings like Hong Leong Building, City House and Shenton House are also seen in the background. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Site Photographs, 62
creator: NA
description: This site photograph was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Choa Chu Kang Housing Development Board Estate along Choa Chu Kang North 6 : General View, 9
creator: NA
description: A general view of the 607-unit HDB estate in Choa Chu Kang along Choa Chu Kang North 6. This is a design and build project undertaken by Akitek Tenggara and led by Tay Kheng Soon. The design team introduced many groundbreaking design considerations for a HDB estate such as greater block depth to increase density and reduce block length, a central entrace to create a strong identity, column structure to allow for maximum flexibility for room layout, a central communal open space and underground car parks to minimise street noise and hazardous vehicular traffic, children's play areas and covered access from the car parks to all lift lobbies.

title: Seletar East Camp during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.SELETAR EAST CAMPAs part of the national effort to stem the spread of COVID-19 in the dormitories, healthy migrant workers were moved into unused Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) camps. Seletar East Camp was one of these camps. Working closely with the SAF, #TeamNUH quickly operationalised a medical post in this camp in May 2020 within 72 hours. The team also carried out swabbing and serology work there. The team ceased operations at the camp on 8 July 2020."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Research Process : Miscellaneous Documents, Drawings, Plans and Photographs, 67
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a research material from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Setting up of Expo Community Care Facility for COVID-19 patients before start of circuit breaker period [2]
creator: Creator:Dennis Chew Yin Sang
description: "A very tiring and emergency express work to build tentages for Singapore EXPO hall 1 to hall 10 in 3 days. Our workers have to get special clearance from MTI & MOM before we can start work during the peak of Covid19 pandemic. We had on-site recce of Singapore EXPO Hall 1 to Hall 6 on the 9th April 2020. We completed the tentage setup by 12nd April 2020. Then there is another calling to build tentage for EXPO Hall 7 to Hall 10 on the 22nd April 2020. We required urgent approval from MTI and MOM for our workers to be able to work onsite. It was a challenging time and we have to thanks Surbana Jurong Consultants Pte Ltd to expedite getting approval for us to commence work."--Contributed by Dennis Chew Yin Sang, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows tents set up by Event Business Management Pte Ltd outside Hall 3 of Singapore EXPO before the start of circuit breaker. The tents will serve as Expo Community Care Facility for COVID-19 patients. A mobile ultrasound van can be seen inside one of the tents. Additional description by Library staff. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Site Photographs, 27
creator: NA
description: This site photograph was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Grand Hotel, 1967 : side view [1]
creator: NA
description: This 1967 photograph shows a side view of one of the buildings of Grand Hotel, located at Still Road South. The Victorian-style building has architectural features like Corinthian columns, decorative arches and plaster facade decorations. The octagonal structure at one end of the building and a balcony with iron lacework railings are depicted in the picture. Grand Hotel, a Victorian-style complex was built in 1917 and used as a private residence by Moona Kadir Sultan, a wealthy Indian merchant. The complex was then-named Karikal Mahal, after the merchant’s hometown of Karikal in Tamil Nadu (India). Grand Hotel itself was established in 1947 and closed in 2000. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Sarimbun Scout Camp : Scouts, 15
creator: NA
description: Scouts at the Sarimbun Scout Camp located at Jalan Bahtera, off Lim Chu Kang Road. This 12-hectare campsite provides a rural enclave for local scouts. Its design is reminiscent of the ambiguous boundaries associated with vernacular kampong architecture. Completed in phases from 1986 to 1996 by Akitek Tenggara, with Tay Kheng Soon leading the design team, the campsite was initially made up of an assembly hall, a canteen, a dormitory, and 3 washrooms. In the later years, more structures were added, including a 7-storey high steel tower and A-frame timber huts.

title: Graves : general view [1]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1993 photograph shows a family mourning at their parents' graves at a cemetery, during Qing Ming Jie. Qing Ming (Cheng Beng in dialect) is All Souls' Day for the Chinese. It is a time to remember the departed and to pay respect to one's deceased ancestors and family members. As it emphasises filial piety, Qing Ming is a major Chinese festival with many Chinese visiting the cemeteries of relatives. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Landscape and Streetscape of Singapore. Chinatown/Ann Siang Hill, 2
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a street in Chinatown. It is taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1985 photograph depicts a block at Lavender Street (at Hamilton Road corner). Lavender Street was named in 1858. At that time, the smell of the area was unbearable due to the urine and nightsoil used to fertilise the Chinese vegetable gardens. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Orthogonal Model, 35
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the orthogonal model of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP). In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Lorong 28 Geylang, towards Geylang Road, 1992 : general view
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1992 photograph depicts Lorong 28 Geylang, looking from the east side towards Geylang Road. It shows the view of a one-way street with shophouses on both sides of the road, and roadside parking lots. There are vehicles parked in some of the parking lots. The foreground of the photograph shows a two storey building with shophouses, fringed by trees. A three storey building and and a block of flats can be seen in the background of the photograph. Geylang is believed to be a corruption of the term "kilang", Malay for factory, from the coconut and lemongrass processing factories of the area. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Disinfection of a tent at Westlite Woodlands workers' dormitory during phase 1 re-opening [6]
creator: Creator:Anonymous
description: "This is a picture of my colleague at work. These photos are the disinfection process by my colleague in a full PPE suit and a booster equipment. We work for ORIGIN Exterminators. We are disinfecting in foreign worker dormitory and also tentages that houses those with confirmed covid 19 cases. The workers are requested to move to another location while the disinfection is in process. They have to wait until it is done before they can go back, as the disinfection chemical are not recommended to be inhaled and also it can cause skin irritation. After disinfection, a cloth will be used to wipe down the chemical. Then the workers will go back to their dormitory and wait for further instruction from their dormitory officers."--Contributed by Anonymous, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a close-up view of a man in white protective clothing, disinfecting rows of beds in a large white tent located at Westlite Woodlands, a workers' dormitory. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Nanyang Technological University, Hall of Residence No. V : Model, 1
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing the model of Nanyang Technological University's Hall of Residence No. V. The building is designed for tropical living. It is made up of four rectangular residential blocks, a foyer and a dinnig hall. Each residential block can house up to 125 students and has a central courtyard. These buildings are built with a robust concrete frame that is clearly defined. The spaces between the concrete frames are filled with glazed metal windows, which are positioned behind the frame to create partial shade. Moreover, a significant recess is incorporated beneath the windows to enable proper air circulation within the rooms. This architectural approach can be likened to the modern version of the traditional 'monsoon window' concept. While all four residential blocks share a similar basic layout, they are distinguished by the varying colors of the panels located behind the windows.

title: Making of "And miles to flow"- a 35mm documentary, photograph 19
creator: NA
description: NA
abstract: சாந்தா ரதி ஒரு பன்முகத்தன்மை கொண்டவர். அவர் ஒரு நடனக் கலைஞர், ஆசிரியர், நடன இயக்குனர், கலாச்சார ஆர்வலர் மற்றும் திரைப்படத் தயாரிப்பாளர். அவர் இந்தியா மற்றும் சிங்கப்பூரின் மிகச் சிறந்த நடன குருக்களின் கீழ் பிரத்தியேக பயிற்சி பெற்றவர். Photos capture the making of documentary film And miles to flow. It highlights the kinship in spirit shared by Kathakali of India with Noh and Kabuki of Japan and Chinese Opera with Kathakali occupying the centre stage. She has scripted, directed and produced the film. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Landscape and Streetscape of Singapore. Marina Square Case Study, 33
creator: NA
description: This photograph of the Marina Square area was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Maps and Plans, 35
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a plan from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Spottiswoode Park Road shophouses : general view [9]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This is a 1982 photograph of the exterior of 2 shophouses located at Spottiswoode Park Road. Spottiswoode Park Road, which is near the Tanjong Pagar area, is probably named after one of the partners of Spottiswoode & Co. They were William, Charles and Archibald Spottiswoode. One of the shophouse is 2 storey high, while the other is 3 storey, with recessed entrances. These buildings seem to belong to the Early Shophouse style, with 2 or 3 French wooden windows on the upper floors. A truck is parked in front of one of the shophouses. Two women can be seen in front of one of the shophouse and seem to be tidying, up as a dustpan can be seen outside the shophouse. A sheet of cloth is also stretched out on a frame off the doorway of the shop. Title devised by Library staff.

title: I Light Marina Bay, A Blue Mirage in the City of Light : general view
creator: NA
description: This 2010 photograph shows a lighting sculpture titled "A Blue Mirage in the City of Light" by WY-To architects. It depicts a gem that reflects light from both the natural and artificial light sources present at Marina Bay. 16 ensembles of 2-metre tall 20/20 laminated glass are installed, offset and rotated along two facing lines. One external side of each glazing ensemble is highly reflective, while the PVB interlayer has a specific polarizing treatment. Be it day or night, the installation creates prismatic reflections of the surrounding cityscape. Title devised by Library staff.

description: This photograph shows a close-up of a woman in front of an altar during a Hungry Ghost Festival celebration organised by 植物园小贩住宅联合社. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Computer Generated Drawings, 5
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a computer generated drawings from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Aerial view of Civic District, 2000
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows an aerial view of the Civic District. On the bottom left is the Boat Quay area, and across the river at the bottom right is the Asian Civilisations Museum (ACM), which is next to the Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall, with its clock tower rising above the rest of the buildings in the vicinity. Moving up the river to the left, the former Hill Street Station with its domed roof can be seen along Hill Street. Across it is the High Street Centre. Spanning over the Singapore River is the historic Elgin Bridge on North Bridge Road. Moving up the road on the right is the Parliament House. Next to the Parliament House, facing St Andrew's road, is the former City Hall, and across the road is The Padang. Further up St Andrew's Road is the grounds of Saint Andrew's Cathedral, with its distinctive spire visible among some trees. Further up the road at the intersection with Stamford Road is the Raffles City Convention Centre with the tallest building being the Swissotel The Stamford. Dwarfed by the hotel, is the Singapore Recreation Club building at The Padang. Behind it, The War Memorial Park with its distinctive cenotaph sits next to Nicoll Highway on the right. Across the highway is the Suntec City. Title devised by Library staff. Description by Library staff.

title: Stay Well packs for National Kidney Foundation (NKF) patients at Admiralty Dialysis Centre
creator: Creator:Be Kind SG
description: "Since early 2019, Be Kind SG has created micro-volunteering opportunities at National Kidney Foundation (NKF) dialysis centres. These sessions usually include a #craftforgood session where volunteers craft flower arrangements and various crafts to present at a short befriending session. Due to the pandemic, we were unable to volunteer in-person at NKF. Instead, our lead volunteers, Jackie and Swee Luan, have created various stay well packs for dialysis patients at Admiralty and Bukit Batok Dialysis Centres in June and September separately. Other volunteers created beautiful handmade encouragement cards to pack into the care packs. The pandemic has made us think of volunteering in creative and innovative ways."--Contributed by Be Kind SG, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Administering a COVID-19 swab test during phase 2 of re-opening
creator: Creator:Dr William Tan
description: "The most common COVID-19 test is a “nasopharyngeal swab, which involves extracting a viral sample from the nasopharynx — the space between the upper part of the throat and the very back of the nose — and analyzing those results in a lab”. Nobody likes to have their nasopharynx probed. “Sticking a long, thin swab several inches deep into this chamber of secretions is surprisingly disagreeable, momentarily painful, or downright excruciating”. The experience of getting a Covid-19 test has been described as having your brain “tickled,” or, alternatively, “stabbed” (though it never actually touches your brain). Some says it’s more like “laughing soda out of your nose — that warm, fizzy feeling” or as if “you were swimming and you get chlorine all the way back there.” It’s a difficult area to swab. Sticking anything far enough up the nose is likely to trigger sneezing, coughing, and tears. In this photo, my patient was fearful at the start. When I inserted the swab into his nose, he fell backward, his legs started kicking, his left hand waved for me to stop, as if he is in an electric chair. I realised that fear can bring about such reaction, hence I have to separate the pain from fear. I started preparing my patients mentally before inserting the swab into their noses so that they are not caught off guard such as providing an overview of the technique before the test begins, talking them through the insertion process, and counting down the seconds during the swab. What a relief for me and for my patients that a Covid-19 test, no matter how uncomfortable, only lasts a few seconds."--Contributed by Dr William Tan, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows a doctor administering a COVID-19 swab test to a patient during phase 2 of re-opening. The doctor can be seen inserting a swab into the nose of a patient. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Wind Tunnel Test, 7
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a wind tunnel test being conducted as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Seletar East Camp during COVID-19 pandemic
creator: NA
description: "THANK YOU NUHEROES. Singapore reported its first confirmed case of COVID-19 on 23 January 2020. In response, the National University Hospital (NUH) ramped up its efforts to support our nation’s battle against COVID-19. In addition to ensuring the hospital continues running smoothly while responding to the rapidly developing global situation, over 500 staff from NUH went above and beyond by stepping forward to volunteer to care for migrant workers at the dormitories and a community care facility.SELETAR EAST CAMPAs part of the national effort to stem the spread of COVID-19 in the dormitories, healthy migrant workers were moved into unused Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) camps. Seletar East Camp was one of these camps. Working closely with the SAF, #TeamNUH quickly operationalised a medical post in this camp in May 2020 within 72 hours. The team also carried out swabbing and serology work there. The team ceased operations at the camp on 8 July 2020."--Contributed by National University Hospital, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call.

title: Jalan Eunos Avenue 4, from Jalan Eunos Service Reservoir : general view [7]
creator: NA
description: This 1992 photograph shows Jalan Eunos Avenue 4, with a view from Jalan Eunos Service Reservoir and Booster Station. The old service reservoir supplements and provides backup water supply for the eastern regions of Singapore and stores water mainly from Bedok Reservoir. Both Jalan Eunos Avenue 4 and the Jalan Eunos Service Reservoir are not found in the present day street directory. Jalan Eunos was named after Mohammed Eunos Abdullah, the father of Malay journalism and first editor of Utusan Melayu. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Spottiswoode Park Road shophouses : general view [7]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This is a 1982 photograph of the exterior of two shophouses located at Spottiswoode Park Road. Spottiswoode Park Road, which is near the Tanjong Pagar area, is probably named after one of the partners of Spottiswoode & Co. They were William, Charles and Archibald Spottiswoode. One of the shophouse is two-storey high, while the other is three-storey, with recessed entrances. These buildings seem to belong to the Early Shophouse style, with two or three French wooden windows on the upper floors. A truck parked in front of one of the shophouses can be partially seen. A sheet of cloth is also stretched out on a frame off the doorway of the shop. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Chancery Lodge : Construction, 6
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing Chancery Lodge being constructed. Completed in 1986, Chancery Lodge is made up of eight split-level townhouses arranged in an L-shaped layout. Embracing tropical architectural influences, the design features of the condominium include inclining roofs, extensive overhanging eaves, jack-roofs, timber mesh screens that effectively diffuse sunlight, and a network of trellis beams designed to offer shade.

title: Holland Village, at Lorong Liput : general view [2]
creator: NA
description: This 1992 photograph depicts commercial buildings at Holland Village at Lorong Liput. Holland Village was once an exclusive European expatriate centre for the rich, particularly during the British military presence. Today, the village with public and private housing estates and its distinctive 'Enterolobium Saman', tall large shady raintrees with monkey pods and crimson or pink flowers, remains as a popular entertainment hangout for both 'yuppies' and expatriates. title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Research Process : Miscellaneous Documents, Drawings, Plans and Photographs, 2
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows a plan from the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: I Light Marina Bay, "My Public Garden" : general view [1]
creator: NA
description: This 2010 photograph shows a lighting sculpture titled "My Public Garden" by TILT (France). "My Public Garden" is a luxurious glowing garden, a playful and festive park full of fanciful plants and enchanted flowers. A total of 29 giant plant-like light sculptures of 6 different varieties will make up the bouquets adorning the site. Marina Bay will be transformed into an imaginary landscape from an artist's sketchbook, where giant wild plants bloom in the darkness, glowing softly with an elegant luminosity. It is an enchanted forest, beckoning the public to enjoy an intimate stroll among the immense, alluring bouquets. The light sculptures are large artworks, the smallest being 3.5m tall & the largest at 11m, visible from far away, creating a beautiful landscape even from a distance, offering an interplay of perspectives. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Two girls hugging the night before circuit breaker period
creator: Creator:Lester Ledesma
description: “My daughter Leanne says goodbye to her next door playmate Karly, whom she won't be seeing again for at least a month as Singapore prepares to fight the pandemic with its "Circuit Breaker" measures. On the night before lockdown took effect, we let the kids play at home till late. Two hours before midnight, they hugged tightly for a few heartbreaking minutes before Karly headed out the door." Photographer’s statement: "Staying in lockdown is hard, but being in lockdown with two kids while working and parenting is even harder. As a freelance photojournalist, I am used to traveling the world and documenting the lives of others. COVID-19 put all this on hold, and like everyone else in Singapore I was stuck at home during Phase 1 CB. For over two months my wife and I lived, loved, worked and raised our kids within the four walls of our apartment. It's an emotional roller coaster ride replete with joys, frustrations and no small amount of hardship. My parents and grandparents lived through the Japanese occupation, and as a child I remember joining the anti-Marcos 'revolution' with my siblings back in the Philippines. I see the pandemic as something similar - a great upheaval that will have a profound effect on my own family years to come. For my kids and for posterity, I decided to document in earnest our lockdown experience. They may be too young to remember this god-awful pandemic (my daughter was 6, my son was 10 months old then), but I hope this pictorial account will serve as a record of what our family endured together. Most photos you see here are bright and sunny. Many accounts of life in lockdown tend to be dreary and depressing, but I beg to differ. As parents, my wife and I believe it is our responsibility to have a positive outlook during these trying times. We owe it to our kids to keep life fun, interesting, and as normal as it can get. Or maybe it was their presence that kept the light warm and shining within these four walls. Whatever the case may be, this lockdown experience is one that will always help define our family."--Contributed by Lester Ledesma, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows two girls hugging the night before circuit breaker period. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Johnston's Pier, S'pore 4, in 1890s : general view
creator: Lambert, G. R.
description: This 1890s photograph from G.R. Lambert & Co. shows Johnston's Pier at Collyer Quay. Built in 1855, Johnston's Pier was named after Alexander Johnston, a doyen of the European mercantile community who founded the firm A.C. Johnston & Co. Gharries, or horse-drawn carriages, could be spotted along the pier, but by 1880 they were replaced by rickshaws, which became an overwhelmingly popular mode of transportation. Johnston’s Pier was demolished in 1933, only to be replaced by Clifford Pier. Title from inscription, on front of photograph. Information contributed by Richard Hale.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Research Process : Miscellaneous Documents, Drawings, Plans and Photographs, 54
creator: NA
description: This photograph was taken for the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Chinese family in Sungei Lui village, Raub, Pahang
creator: NA
description: A photograph taken during the Health Week Competition in Sungei Lui Village, Raub, April 1954. A Chinese family, including mother and five children, outside a wooden house in Sungei Lui village. Spring Festival couplets affixed vertically on each side of a door as a Spring Festival decoration. This photograph is part of Mrs Jean Marshall collection of photographs taken between 1953 and 1954 when Jean Mary Gray was a British Red Cross field officer in West Pahang during the Malayan Emergency. In 1961, she became Jean Mary Marshall when she married David Marshall, Singapore's first elected Chief Minister. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : The Team Behind the Project, 4
creator: NA
description: This photograph shows the people involved in the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Raffles College building : general view [6]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1995 photograph shows one of the bungalows built in Art Deco style which was used to house academic staff of the former Raffles College at the Bukit Timah campus. It is one of the 5 bungalows gazetted for conservation.  Established at the Bukit Timah site in 1929, Raffles College (with King Edward VII College of Medicine) was incorporated as the University of Malaya in 1949. In 1962, this university became known as the University of Singapore, and later renamed the National University of Singapore (N.U.S.) when it merged with Nanyang University in 1980. Today, this campus is home to the N.U.S.'s Law Faculty, the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy and five Research Institutes. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Joo Chiat Road no. 408 : exterior [2]
creator: Lee, Kip Lin
description: This 1984 photograph depicts the façade of a typical traditional shophouse located at the corner of Fowlie Road. The shophouse no. 408 Joo Chiat Road, is one of a row of terrace houses. The two-storey shophouse features windows with wooden louvred shutters on the upper floor. The façade is recessed at the ground level, forming a’ five foot way”. The ground floor also spots a pair of swing doors and windows on either side. The building is supported by columns. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan : Landscape and Streetscape of Singapore. Marina Square Case Study, 27
creator: NA
description: This photograph of the Marina Square area was taken as part of the Kampong Bugis Development Guide Plan (DGP) project. In 1989, Tay Kheng Soon led a team under the auspices of the Singapore Insitute of Architects to propose how the 72 hectares Kampong Bugis area should be redeveloped. In his DGP, Tay tested the Tropical City Concept by introducing ideas such as high-level shading, horizontal and vertical greening, and tax incentives to reward developers who adopted environmentally friendly building technologies and building design practices. Although Tay's proposed DGP was recongised by the planning authorities for being forward looking in 1991, it was deemed too radical to be implemented at the time.

title: Meal served during quarantine at Hilton Singapore Orchard [3]
alternative: Returning Singaporean student's flight and quarantine experience during Phase Two [8]
creator: Creator:Rebecca Tan Hui Qing
description: "Food served during the stay in Hilton Singapore. When the Singapore government announced that it would mandate a 2-week Stay-Home Notice at designated facilities for individuals arriving from specific countries, I was sitting in my apartment in Los Angeles. Having opted to ride out the pandemic there instead of returning home and finishing my last university classes from 15 hours away, I told myself, “Okay. You just have to be very careful and not get sick. If all goes well, you’ll be able to graduate, return, and relax for two weeks.” Thankfully, things went as planned – not an easy statement to make during these unprecedented times. I completed my final examinations, said goodbye to the friends I had made over four wonderful years, and got on the June 17 flight from Los Angeles to Singapore. The flight went smoothly, being only about 20% full. We were provided face masks, sanitizer and antiseptic wipes. I enjoyed the delicious airplane food, got as much sleep as I could and felt a little surge of happiness at the thought of two weeks of relaxation ahead. After exiting the plane, all passengers turned in health declaration forms and passed through immigration, after which we were brought onto buses heading to a hotel, name unspecified till right after the ride began. When the lady in front of me told me we were heading to the Hilton Singapore, I rejoiced! For two weeks, I slept on luxurious sheets on a huge bed instead of the small bunk bed in my former apartment. Even the toiletries provided were high-class, such as $35 body wash. Free of the demands of schoolwork, I watched a good amount of Netflix and video-called my friends, all of whom were excited to see my quarantine surroundings. I also enjoyed the scrumptious food served three times a day, with occasional snacks left outside my door. While this experience was accompanied by ICA officers’ intermittent visits, as well as video and phone calls to verify my presence in the room, I thought these were justified in the name of ensuring public health and safety. On day 11 of my quarantine, I had to undergo a compulsory Covid-19 test. Despite feeling well, I was still a little worried about the results. However, it was also going to be my first time smelling fresh air in nearly two weeks, so I was excited for – of all things – my visit to Jurong Polyclinic. During the taxi ride there, I stared out of the window, enjoying the verdant greenery and warm weather. Fortunately, I tested negative for Covid-19, completed my staycation and then went home to my family. The pandemic has undeniably taken a big mental toll on many people and every day, I wish the disease could just be wiped out instantly. In the face of such circumstances, I try to think of happy times like this one, where I got to have a staycation I could otherwise never afford, and was carefree enough to soak in each moment."--Contributed by Rebecca Tan Hui Qing, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows breakfast served at Hilton Singapore Orchard where returning students were required to serve their 2-week Stay-Home Notice. The students were recalled during phase 1 of re-opening. The food consists of omelettes, tater tots, sausages and cherry tomatoes served in a box. Drinks and yoghurt are also part of the meal. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.

title: Cheras Housing : Construction, 2
creator: NA
description: A photograph showing a group of people inspecting the construction of the Cheras housing project in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. This development is a low-rise, low-cost housing project that Tay Kheng Soon undertook in mid-1970s. Comprising 676 two-storey houses built for the lower income groups, it is located on a 4.79 hectares site. The original sale price of each unit was M$5000 and each of them has a 13 square metres garden. The houses are arranged in straight lines to catch the prevailing wind, and are arranged in back-to-back clusters of four units around a 2.5 metre wide 'breezeway'. The project was suggested by then Prime Minister of Malaysia Tun Abdul Razak in 1975 who wanted to build low cost houses for the low income group in urban areas.

title: Toothbrushes and cutleries used during stay-home notice (SHN)
creator: Creator:Tan Kai Li
description: "Storing toothbrushes and utensils in the fridge for hygiene purpose. Having returned to Singapore from the US, our family of 4 was to fulfil our Stay Home Notice (SHN) at a designated hotel. As we have young children with us, we prepared for the SHN as though we were preparing for a ''glamping" trip. In order to minimise mess from mealtimes and to ensure we could be as comfortable "living" in the hotel room as possible, we packed extra portable furniture and a whole luggage full of activities, worksheets, craft materials to keep the kids occupied. We had some unwanted roommates (i.e. cockroaches) for the first week of our stay. However, we understood that this was probably unavoidable since hotel rooms were not designed for extended stay without regular housekeeping anyway. The hotel did their best to rectify the problem, but it still took a while before we stop seeing any more roaches. Despite that, our spirits were kept high by the ability to order in our local delights and hawker fares to satisfy our cravings -- something we had missed dearly during our time in the US. Over time, as we recovered from our jetlag, we also turned the hotel room into a classroom filled with painting, clay works, games, learning exercises etc. We are grateful for the comfortable stay, delicious meals and clean linens the hotel staff had worked diligently to provide us. And despite having to stay indoors for 2 weeks, the kids had adjusted well. We also understood from the hotel staff that they were thankful for the SHN bookings as the lack of tourists meant the hotel staff would otherwise be out of work. It takes immense vision, coordination and trust in our system for the SHN arrangements to be affected so seamlessly. Having witnessed how haphazard the Covid19 management was in the States, we are really thankful to be home."--Contributed by Tan Kai Li, as part of the "Documenting COVID-19 in Singapore" collection community call. This photograph shows the inside of a fridge where toothbrushes and cutleries are stored by a family confined to a hotel room while serving out their stay-home notice (SHN). All returning Singaporeans had to serve two weeks of SHN during the pandemic. Additional description by Library staff. Title devised by Library staff.
